title: International Temple, Supreme Assembly, Order of the Rainbow for Girls
teaser: Visiting Rainbow’s international headquarters on the way home from Supreme Session in Tucson.
body: On the drive home from the Supreme Session in Tucson, Arizona (held at El Conquistador Tucson, A Hilton Resort), we stopped in McAlester to visit the International Temple, Supreme Assembly, Order of the Rainbow for Girls.

The Order of the Rainbow for Girls was founded in McAlester on April 6, 1922, by Rev. W. Mark Sexson. The temple was built in 1950–1951 as the Order’s international headquarters and was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2013.
Read the full road trip →

title: Grand Lodge of Connecticut & Columbia Lodge No. 25
alt: George with the Worshipful Master of Columbia Lodge No. 25
teaser: Touring the Grand Lodge of Connecticut, then a Master Mason Degree at Columbia Lodge No. 25.
body: Masonic fellowship, one of the noble traditions of our Craft. This past June I had the great pleasure of touring the Grand Lodge of Connecticut, afterwards the RW Grand Secretary Robert G. Fitzgerald invited me to attend a Master Mason Degree at his Lodge, Columbia Lodge No. 25 A.F. & A.M. in South Glastonbury, Connecticut.
I was warmly welcomed by WM Michael E. Hudson and by my Connecticut brothers. I had a very enjoyable evening, one I’m sure to remember for many years to come.
I highly recommend taking the time to fellowship whenever possible, the gain is sometimes immeasurable.
Photo from the website of Columbia Lodge No. 25.

title: Grand Lodge of Texas
alt: George outside the Grand Lodge of Texas
teaser: “I have to say this building lives up to its namesake, it was a Grand Lodge.”
body: “I have to say this building lives up to its namesake, it was a Grand Lodge. They hold their annual meeting in the auditorium, which seats 4,000. When you enter the front door you are greeted by two statues of Great Masons of Texan history. … If you turn right it will take you to the Grand Lodge Offices & Library (Bro Bruce does a great tour). Down stairs is a nice museum.”
